raw.headline: Playback should get next quarter's product effort, ahead of Access, Usability, and Billing/support
raw.memo_markdown:
## Recommendation
Prioritize Playback next quarter. Playback has {{C021}} complaints with a combined severity of {{C022}}, the largest count and severity total of any area, covering {{C024}} of complaints. Its two issues are `playback/crash_freeze` (rank {{C010}}, priority {{C009}}) and `playback/stops_pausing` (rank {{C020}}, priority {{C019}}).

## Evidence
`playback/crash_freeze` has {{C006}} complaints, a severity sum of {{C007}}, and a mean severity of {{C008}}. `playback/stops_pausing` has {{C016}} complaint with a severity of {{C017}}. Review text describes apps that crash on open and music that stops when the screen turns off. These are self-selected public complaints, not measured usage.

## Alternatives considered
Access ranks first on a single issue. `access/login_failure` has {{C001}} complaints, a severity sum of {{C002}}, and a priority score of {{C004}}. Access overall has {{C025}} complaints, severity {{C026}}, and mean severity {{C027}}, the highest mean of any area, but fewer total complaints than Playback. Access is a credible second choice if leadership weights severity per complaint over total volume, since login failures block account access entirely.

Usability has {{C029}} complaints and severity {{C030}}, with a mean severity of {{C031}}. Its only issue, `usability/ads`, is the lowest-severity item in this set. Billing/support has no mapped complaint records in this analysis, so it cannot be compared on this data.
